html:
The deadliest Atlantic hurricane on record, which struck the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean in October 1780 and killed more than 20,000 people.

The storm hit Barbados on 10 October and nearly flattened it, stripping bark from trees and destroying almost every house. It then passed over Saint Lucia, Martinique and Sint Eustatius, and later Puerto Rico and Hispaniola. Many of the dead were enslaved people on the sugar islands, whose huts gave little shelter.

It came in the middle of the American Revolutionary War, when Britain, France and Spain were fighting over the Caribbean. Both British and French fleets lost ships and thousands of sailors. Two other deadly hurricanes struck the region the same month, which made October 1780 one of the worst months in the history of the islands.

No Atlantic storm since, not even Hurricane Katrina, has killed as many people.
sum: The deadliest Atlantic hurricane on record, which struck the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean in October 1780 and killed more than 20,000 people.
